name: Back up GitHub repositories with Amazon S3 and email reports

parameters.content:
## Back up GitHub repositories with Amazon S3 and email reports

Backs up every repository you own, or an organisation's, into your own S3 bucket every night. Old archives are removed after your retention window, and you get a report email after every run, including the quiet ones.

### How it works
1. Validates your settings before anything runs.
2. Works out the account from your GitHub token, or uses the owner you set, then lists every repository page by page, so large accounts are not cut off at 100.
3. Downloads and uploads one repository at a time as `prefix/repo-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz`. A failed repo is retried, then reported, and the run carries on.
4. Deletes archives under your prefix older than `retention_days`.
5. Emails a summary of what was backed up, skipped, failed and removed.

### Setup steps
- Create a private S3 bucket and an IAM user allowed `s3:ListBucket`, `s3:GetBucketLocation`, `s3:PutObject`, `s3:AbortMultipartUpload` and `s3:DeleteObject`.
- Attach a **GitHub** credential to the three HTTP Request nodes (`repo` scope for private repos), an **AWS** credential to the three S3 nodes and an **SMTP** credential to the email node.
- In **Set Backup Parameters** set `s3_bucket` and `notify_email` (`notify_from` is optional). Leave `github_owner` blank to back up your own account.
- Run it once by hand before relying on the nightly schedule.

### Customization
Change the time in **When Nightly at 2 AM**, the prefix and retention in **Set Backup Parameters**, or send the report to Slack instead of email.

Full bucket and IAM walkthrough: [datadrifter.io setup guide](https://datadrifter.io/github-backup-s3-bucket-iam-setup/)

Made by DataDrifter.

## Schedule and settings

Starts the workflow on the nightly schedule, defines backup configuration values, and validates that required settings are not still placeholders.

## Discover GitHub repositories

Identifies whether the configured GitHub owner is a user or organization, then lists the repositories that should be backed up.

## Back up each repository

One repository at a time: downloads its archive from GitHub, uploads it to Amazon S3 and records the result before moving to the next.

## Apply retention cleanup

Lists existing S3 backups for the repository, filters objects older than the retention window, conditionally deletes expired backups, and passes cleanup activity onward for reporting.

## Report backup results

Aggregates activity across all loop iterations and sends an email report with the backup and cleanup summary.

nodes.name: When Nightly at 2 AM
nodes.notes: Change the cron expression to suit. Test with the manual trigger first.

nodes.name: Set Backup Parameters
nodes.notes: The only node you must edit. Leave github_owner BLANK to back up your own account - it is read from the token. Fill it in only for an organisation or another user. notify_from may be blank; the report is then sent from notify_email.

nodes.name: Validate Backup Settings
nodes.notes: Stops the run before any work if Backup settings still holds a shipped placeholder. you@example.com is reserved: relays accept it and discard it, so without this check a misconfigured template produces green runs and silence forever.

nodes.name: Fetch GitHub Account Info
nodes.notes: Works out who we are backing up so you do not have to say. A blank github_owner asks your token who it belongs to; a filled one is looked up to learn whether it names a user or an organisation, and the next node routes itself accordingly.

nodes.name: List GitHub Repos
nodes.notes: Paginated, so it does not silently stop at 100 repositories. The URL routes itself: an organisation goes to /orgs, your own account goes to /user/repos so PRIVATE repos are included, and another user's account goes to /users/<login>/repos, which GitHub restricts to public repos.

nodes.name: Process Each Repository
nodes.notes: One at a time keeps peak memory to a single archive.

nodes.name: Download Repo Archive
nodes.notes: One unreachable repo must not abandon the whole backup. Failures leave by the ERROR branch (the lower output) carrying GitHub's own message, and are counted in the report. Do NOT set alwaysOutputData here: with an error branch it would push an empty item down the success branch, and S3 would then report 'no binary file data' instead of the real reason.

nodes.name: Upload Archive to S3
nodes.notes: Key is prefix/repo-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz. FLAT on purpose: the S3 node always lists with delimiter='/', so anything in a per-repo subfolder is invisible to the retention step and would never be deleted. Copies still group by repository when sorted, because the name leads.

nodes.name: List S3 Backups
nodes.notes: Runs after the loop finishes, so it sees today's uploads too. Always outputs data: on an empty bucket a node that emits nothing stops the branch, and the run would end here with no report.

nodes.name: Filter Expired Backups
nodes.notes: Deletes nothing itself. It only decides what is out of date.

nodes.name: Check Expired Backups
nodes.notes: Guards the delete node. Without this, a run with nothing to expire would send an item with no key to S3 - and a DELETE with an empty key addresses the BUCKET, not an object. The false branch carries straight on to the report.

nodes.name: Delete Expired Backup
nodes.notes: A failed delete costs storage. It must never abandon the report.

nodes.name: Send Backup Report Email
nodes.notes: Attach your SMTP credential. notify_from may be left blank, in which case the report is sent from notify_email. Whichever is used must be an address your SMTP server is allowed to send as, or the report silently never arrives.

nodes.name: Log Repository Backup Status
nodes.notes: Every repository ends up here exactly once, whether it uploaded or failed. Also separates an EMPTY repository (no commits - nothing to back up) from a real failure, so the failure count keeps meaning something instead of raising the same unfixable alarm every night.

parameters.content:
### Deletes files
Removes EVERYTHING under your prefix older than `retention_days`, whatever put it there. Give this workflow its own prefix.
